subject: Media Literacy
title: Selection Bias: What Gets Covered
description: A quick, practical guide to Selection Bias: What Gets Covered.

hook.text: A plane crash kills 200 people and dominates the news. Malaria kills 2,000 the same day. No mention.

buildup.text: Selection bias occurs when media consistently covers certain stories while ignoring others of equal importance.

discovery.text: Dramatic, unusual, and local events get covered more than slow, systemic, and distant problems.

twist.text: What's not covered shapes public perception as much as what is. Absence of coverage is itself a message.

climax.text: The news creates a distorted map of reality. The biggest issues often get the least coverage.

punchline.text: What isn't in the news is often more important than what is.

quiz.question: What is selection bias in media?
options: Consistently covering certain stories while ignoring others of equal importance
